papers.title_en: CellRFT: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Single-Cell Perturbation Modeling
papers.authors: Jie Yan, Li Liu, Hanze Guo, Jiaxin Hu, Houxin He, Xiaoning Qi, Haoran Wang, Cong Li, Zhong-Yuan Zhang, Yong Wang
papers.evidence: 面向单细胞扰动响应预测的强化微调
papers.tldr: 单细胞扰动响应预测对基因功能与疾病机制研究至关重要，但现有模型多优化替代损失，与生物评价指标不一致，拟合更好未必预测更准。为此提出CellRFT，将生物评价作为直接训练反馈，通过策略梯度学习不可微的生成细胞群评价，并用分层奖励聚合整合多个生物奖励。实验表明其可适配不同预训练模型并提升扰动预测，还揭示生物指标间协同或冲突，为评价设计提供新思路。
papers.abstract_en: Predicting cellular responses to perturbations supports the study of gene function, disease mechanisms, and therapeutic strategies. Despite advances in single-cell perturbation modeling, existing models typically optimize surrogate losses that do not directly reflect the biological criteria used for evaluation, so better data fitting need not yield better biological predictions. To address this mismatch, we introduce \textbf{CellRFT}, a reinforcement fine-tuning framework that uses biological evaluation as direct training feedback. CellRFT uses policy-gradient optimization to learn from non-differentiable evaluations of generated cell populations and integrates multiple biological rewards through hierarchical reward aggregation. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate CellRFT's applicability across different pretrained models and effectiveness in improving perturbation prediction, reveal that optimizing one biological criterion can help or hinder others, and show that complementary rewards can improve criteria beyond those directly optimized, offering a way to probe how biological metrics shape model behavior, with the potential to inform evaluation design. Code will be made available.

papers.title_en: One Intervention per Component is Enough: Towards Identifiability in Linear Stochastic Dynamics from Steady State
papers.evidence: 从基因扰动干预的稳态数据中恢复动力学参数
papers.tldr: 本文研究从稳态观测与干预数据中恢复多元OU过程参数的问题，适用于仅能获得稳态快照的基因扰动等场景。作者证明每个漂移图强连通分量只需一次干预，即可在全局缩放意义下识别全部参数。方法先拓扑排序SCC，逐分量分离边际动态并解稳态矩方程，再用正则化最小二乘联合拟合均值与协方差。实验验证了理论，为稳态快照下的参数识别提供依据。
papers.abstract_en: We study the problem of recovering the parameters of a multivariate Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) process from steady-state observational and interventional data. In many applications, such as large-scale gene perturbation experiments, only stationary "snapshot" measurements are available, making standard stochastic differential equation estimation methods that rely on time-series trajectories inapplicable. We first establish an identifiability result: one intervention per strongly connected component (SCC) of the drift graph suffices to recover all OU process parameters generically up to a global scaling factor. This holds provided that the SCC condensation graph is connected with a single root and certain spectral nondegeneracy assumptions hold. We propose a recursive learning algorithm that orders SCCs topologically and, for each component, isolates its marginal dynamics and solves a linear system derived from the steady-state moment equations, leveraging parameters recovered for upstream components. Building on this theoretical foundation, we propose a regularized least-squares estimator that jointly minimizes residuals of the steady-state mean and covariance equations across observational and interventional data. Experimental results validate our theoretical findings in recovering parameters of the underlying OU process.
